conviction_note: The findings net to about -0.5: third-party DAU acceleration and a crowded short (18.2% of float, 8.5 days to cover) on one side; on the other, a bookings ramp the full-year guide quietly needs in Q4 (about +12% y/y implied against +8-9% in Q2/Q3), Max being wound down, and a flagged EBITDA hit from the DAU bonus. This name has sold DAU beats on 5 straight prints because it trades on bookings and the guide, so p_up stays at 50. abs_move_pct is 14.5, slightly above the 13.5% implied move, because a guidance reset (higher DAU guide, lower EBITDA) and possibly a first look at 2027 are likely.

EBITDA guide $76M, from the Q2 shareholder letter, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001562088/000162828026053299/q2fy26duolingo6-30x26share.htm (2026-08-05). Street revenue $303-304.7M and EPS $0.55-0.57 (Earnings Whispers via finviz 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/408330/duolingos-user-rebound-faces-a-test-can-q3-show-bookings-catching-up-to-daus ; Investing.com preview $303M / $0.57). No sourced Q3 bookings or DAU consensus was found. FY26 guide: bookings $1,285M, revenue $1,207M, adj. EBITDA $320M (26.5%). Q2 bookings beat its own guide by 2.0% ($289.1M vs $283.5M), so print_vs_bar assumes a similar beat on the bookings guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,103,345 shares = 18.21% of float, 8.5 days to cover, as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (published 2026-10-26), down 0.7% from the prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/DUOL/short-interest/). That is crowded. The baseline rejected the 25-delta skew as implausible (46.5 vol points), so no usable skew exists. Put/call OI is 0.75 and the ATM spread is 24% of mid. Event-implied move is 13.54% against a median of 13.88% over the last 8 prints, 6 of which were down, including the last 5. Tape: -8.6% over 20 days and -4.2% over 5 days into the print, about -15% from the ~$158 of 2026-09-01 after the upgrade wave, and -49% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: DA Davidson's panel of 170k+ users (note of 2026-10-20) points to Q3 2026 DAU growth of about 26-28% y/y. That compares with management's guide of 'remain above 20%' and Q2's +23%. The panel also shows October still accelerating (+1.3% m/m to date, after September's +3.4%). The firm expects a raised DAU guide and raised its target to $175 from $160.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DAU beats have been sold. Q2 2026: DAU +23% (accelerating), stock -9.41%. Q3 2025: DAU +36%, stock -25.49%. The stock trades on bookings and the guide, not on DAU.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The panel read is public, and the stock rallied on the August read (+7% on 2026-08-18) but has since fallen about 15% from early September to $135. If the market were paying for a DAU beat, the stock would not be at its 20-day lows with 18% of the float short. The specific 26-28% figure is one broker's panel, not consensus.
findings.independence: The same broker's August note put Q3 DAU at +24% from data through Aug 15 (https://coincentral.com/is-duolingo-duol-stock-finally-turning-a-corner-one-analyst-says-yes, 2026-08-18), so this is one data source read twice. Evercore's Mahaney cites chess at 7M DAU in under a year (Investing.com preview).

findings.finding: The full-year bookings guide of $1,285M held, minus H1 actuals ($308.5M + $289.1M) and the Q3 guide ($307M), implies Q4 2026 bookings of about $380M, roughly +12% y/y on a derived Q4 2025 of ~$338M. Q2 grew +8% and Q3 is guided +8.9%. Extended free trials (one to two months) defer conversion. Holding the FY range therefore needs a Q4 reacceleration. Trimming it, or holding it only on a Q3 beat, is the line this stock has sold on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings guidance drove the big moves. Q2 2026: a 2% bookings beat with the FY range held, stock -9.41% on 'cautious bookings guidance'. Q3 2025: Q4 bookings guide, -25.49%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-26): FY26 guide of 10-12% bookings, -14.01%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4-implied number is arithmetic, not a published figure, and previews (e.g. Earnings Whispers 2026-10-26) frame the debate as 'can bookings catch up to DAUs' without quantifying the Q4 ramp. If the market were pricing a Q4 bookings shortfall, sell-side targets would not have been raised through October (Goldman 114 to 135, MS 125 to 140, DA Davidson to 175). Partly priced via the 20-day drawdown.
findings.independence: The Q1 letter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001562088/000162828026029790/q1fy26duolingo3-31x26share.htm) shows FY bookings guided at $1,280M then, now $1,285M: held, not raised, despite the DAU acceleration. Wedbush (2026-09-01) flagged 'only modest bookings growth and unchanged 2026 bookings guidance' (https://stockstotrade.com/news/duolingo-inc-duol-news-2026_09_01/). Same company document as the bar.

findings.finding: Von Ahn said on the Q2 call 'we may actually sunset Max', and at Citi's TMT conference in early September said 'we're not entirely sure what we're going to do with Max'. New subscribers reportedly no longer see Max, and Video Call is moving down into Super. Max is roughly 10% of subs (author's estimate), so the change dilutes revenue per subscriber in the bookings the Q4 guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior reaction to a tier change alone. Moving AI features into lower tiers coincided with the -14.01% (Feb 2026) and -25.49% (Nov 2025) prints, where the stated driver was monetization being deprioritized.
findings.why_not_priced: Management's statements are public, but no quantified hit to revenue per subscriber exists. If it were priced, previews would carry a Max-driven bookings cut; Earnings Whispers lists 'possible sunset' only as a debate item.
findings.independence: The Dolphin Research summary of the Q2 call says Max 'may be discontinued' and describes a cheaper ad-supported tier (https://longportapp.cn/news/295028818). It shares the bookings line with the Q4-ramp finding but rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: A DAU bonus of more than $10M triggers if Q4 DAU growth is at least 25%, and it is excluded from the 26.5% FY adj. EBITDA margin guide. With Q3 DAU tracking at 26-28%, DA Davidson expects the FY EBITDA guide to be cut to about 25.7% margin alongside a raised DAU guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin guides have mattered here: Q2 2026 raised the EBITDA margin by about 1pt and the stock still fell 9.41%. That suggests margin is secondary to bookings.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company disclosed the bonus and the broker flagged the cut in advance. The residual is whether the cut comes larger than $10M or alongside other spend, since 2026 is already called 'heavy on spending' (JPMorgan, 2026-09-01).
findings.independence: The bonus terms are in the Q2 letter and call summaries (search summary of the 2026-08-05 release). It shares a document with the DAU finding, but it is a different line (EBITDA guide, not DAU).

findings.finding: Short interest is 18.21% of float (7.10M shares), 8.5 days to cover, at the 2026-10-15 settlement. The stock fell 8.6% over 20 days and about 15% from its early-September level into the print, so a sold-down, crowded short meets a print with probable DAU upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two up-moves in the last 8 prints were large: +13.75% (Aug 2025) and +21.61% (May 2025). Short interest was about 4.8 days to cover in April 2026 (equibles), so the base has grown into this print.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the bear case already expressed. A neutral or better guide forces cover with 8.5 days of volume short. If the short were being unwound ahead of the print, short interest would be falling materially; it fell only 0.7%.
findings.independence: Equibles' April 2026 figure of 7.6M shares and 4.77 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/duol/shortinterest) shows days to cover rose as volume fell.

findings.finding: CEO Luis von Ahn sold 110,046 shares on 2026-10-07 at an average $151.70 (about $16.7M) under a 10b5-1 plan, which MarketBeat describes as a 50% cut to the reported position. Insiders sold about $37.7M in the last quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to insider sales on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a pre-arranged plan and public on Form 4, so it is mostly priced. It is filed because a 50% cut ahead of a print is a small sentiment negative a judge may weigh differently.
findings.independence: none (single aggregator; Form 4 not separately fetched)

findings.finding: Coursera, the closest listed consumer-edtech peer to report since Duolingo last spoke, beat Q3 revenue on 2026-10-29 ($376.7M vs $364-372M guide) but guided Q4 to about $362M, roughly 2.7% under consensus, and fell about 8%. The market is punishing soft edtech guides this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pattern matches Duolingo's own Q2 2026: beat, cautious guide, -9.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy. Coursera is mostly enterprise and degrees post-Udemy, so the read-through to Duolingo's consumer bookings is weak, and DUOL's 5.4% fall on 2026-10-28 already came with sector selling.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not company-confirmed. Coursera's own release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000068/cour-20260930xexx991.htm

findings.finding: User complaints about the summer 2026 course upgrade scrambling progress were heavy on Reddit, and Android Authority's poll found a 'clear majority' negatively affected (July 2026). A third-party tracker flagged a spike in negative App Store reviews around 2026-06-20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product backlash narratives (the AI-first memo, the energy system) coincided with negative prints in 2025-26, but DAU kept growing through them.
findings.why_not_priced: It is anecdotal, and the broad series (DA Davidson's DAU panel, September +3.4% m/m) points the other way, so it is sized near zero. If it had hit engagement, the panel would show deceleration.
findings.independence: Contradicted in direction by the DA Davidson panel (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/da-davidson-raises-duolingo-stock-price-target-on-dau-growth-trends-93CH-4959643).

findings.finding: A securities class action was filed on 2026-10-07 in W.D. Pa. (City of Dearborn Heights Act 345 Police & Fire v. Duolingo), class period 2025-05-02 to 2026-02-26, with a lead-plaintiff deadline of 2026-12-07. It alleges misstatements on monetization, AI and the sustainability of user growth.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced and immaterial to the print. It is filed only because management may be more conservative on guidance language while litigation is open.

outside_window.finding: Class action lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-12-07; no economic event inside the window.

baseline_tension: The skew is unusable. The DAU evidence and the crowded short cut against the 20-day drawdown and the five straight negative reactions, while the bookings and Q4-ramp evidence agrees with them, so the net is roughly balanced.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the DAU finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6, because DAU beats were sold at -9.4% and -25.5%.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): at 18.2% of float short, the bookings/Q4-ramp finding went from -1.5 to -1.2 and the Max finding from -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy loses to a broad series): the course-complaint finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, because the DAU panel contradicts it in direction.

Left standing: positioning +1.5, EBITDA bonus -0.3, CEO sale -0.2, Coursera proxy -0.3, class action -0.1. The bar is company-sourced, so no cap applied. p_up stays at 50 and abs_move_pct at 14.5. The pre and post sums came out equal at -0.6 and -0.5 only coincidentally; the individual sizes moved.
